title: My husband said he was an only child
author: Storytime
hook: My husband told me he was an only child. At his father's funeral, three men introduced themselves as his brothers.
story: My husband Paul and I have been married for six years. He always said he was an only child. His mom died young, and it was just him and his dad. Paul's dad passed away last month. The funeral was small. Maybe thirty people. Halfway through the service, a man walked up to me and said, you must be Paul's wife. I'm Michael, his brother. I laughed, because I thought it was a joke. Then a second man walked over. Then a third. Same jawline. Same eyes. Same laugh as Paul. Three brothers. All from different states. All with different moms. None of them knew about each other until the funeral either. Except Paul. Paul knew. He knew about every single one. When I asked him in the car why he never told me, he stared at the steering wheel and said, because then I'd have to tell you about the fourth one. Part two?
caption: he said only child. he lied four times 😳 #storytime
sound: a slow, suspenseful piano with a dramatic sting at very low volume
why: Multi-part marriage secret series are among the most viewed storytime formats, the only child claim is the setup, and the fourth one line is a strong cliffhanger for a series.

title: Grandma's secret TikTok account
author: Storytime
hook: My grandma asked me to help her delete a TikTok account. It had four hundred thousand followers.
story: My grandma is eighty-three. She calls her phone the little computer. Last weekend, she asked me to help her delete an app. She said, I made a mistake and I don't know how to get out. I opened TikTok on her phone. Her account had four hundred thousand followers. I almost dropped the phone. She just sat there, sipping her tea, completely calm. The account was anonymous. No face, just her hands and a kitchen table. And every video was the same. Grandma, rating family recipes. Brutally. Zero out of ten, too much salt, my daughter in law has never met a vegetable. Last Thanksgiving's green bean casserole had two million views. It was my mom's. My mom still thinks people loved it. She has no idea it was a roast. I asked her why she wants to delete it. She said, because your aunt Carol found it. And she recognized her own sweet potato pie. Carol is furious. Mom doesn't know yet. But here's the problem. Grandma's followers have been asking for a live stream from Thanksgiving dinner. And Grandma admitted she already said yes. Thanksgiving is in two weeks. Do I help her delete it, or help her go live?
caption: grandma has been rating our food for years 🥧 #storytime
sound: a playful, cheeky kitchen jingle at very low volume
why: Grandparent stories are always popular, the little computer detail makes the follower count hilarious, Thanksgiving recipes tie in seasonally, and the delete or go live question pulls comments.

title: Neighbour's smart speaker hears me
author: Storytime
hook: My downstairs neighbour thinks her flat is haunted. It isn't. It's me.
story: My flat has very thin floors. I can hear my downstairs neighbour, Mrs. Hughes, sneeze. A few weeks ago, I was cooking and said out loud, set a timer for ten minutes. From below, I heard a little voice say, timer set, ten minutes. Her smart speaker. It could hear me through the floor. I should have told her. Instead, I did nothing. For a while. Then one night I said, play some jazz. Downstairs, jazz started playing. I heard her say, oh, how lovely. And honestly, she seemed happy. So it became a thing. I even started saying good night, and the speaker would wish her sweet dreams. Jazz in the evenings. Weather in the mornings. Then last Tuesday, I said, what's on my shopping list? And her speaker read out, eggs, bread, and holy water. I went down to check on her. Her whole hallway was covered in little crosses. She told me, very seriously, that her flat has a friendly ghost. It plays jazz and reminds her about the weather. She's become quite attached to it. She's even named it Harold. Do I tell her Harold is me?
caption: I accidentally became her ghost 👻 #storytime
sound: a gentle, quirky jazz tune at very low volume
why: Thin floors and neighbours are universally relatable, the timer is a funny setup, holy water and Harold the ghost are absurd payoffs, and the confess question gets lots of joke comments.
